relationship view and dashboard coverage view

claims.statement: A click on a Data row opens an explorer of that source.
Opening a source writes no file and does not query a database.
Explorer reuses workspace profiles, Summary and Rows; no second engine.
Progressive disclosure: hover shows field summary (columns, types, distributions); click opens an explorer of field summary plus rows.
Columns and data types are the first thing to answer; then a feel for values and quick views.
Seeing how sources relate and which sources existing dashboards cover is wanted, but is a separate action from the source hover/click (overlaps W5 schema).
Save from the explorer writes an .eda analysis file.
W5 owns the relationship and coverage views. Any per-source used-by marker in W4 reads the usage edges in packages/explorEDA/src/lib/schema/schemaGraph.ts, not a second copy.
Hover card is about a third of the viewport, shows the full-width field summary with scrolling rows, and draws no charts.
The explorer is a dashboard against one source only. Value-click behavior is an agent default, to be corrected by feedback.
Mockup A is the chosen shape. The rail is never the exploration surface; a full all-fields view is a dedicated view (W5).

milestones.title: Click a source to explore it

cut_line: Suggested charts, compact card, rail tree

history.event: Intent recovered from TASK-0092 recording; three approaches compared; question round 1 prepared.

Round 2 recorded. Four mockup variants rendered on the live app with real Runs data (tmp/explorer-mockups, not committed): A hover card + summary-and-rows page, B scratch dashboard, C compact hover + rows-first, D rail column tree + column focus. Default value click filters rows and re-describes columns.

question_rounds.answers: Most important: columns and data types, and a feel for the values. Hover a source shows the existing field Summary. Click switches the main view to a drill-in explorer: field summary, then actual rows fast; from there save or do something else. Persistence undecided (maybe scratch, maybe read-only, maybe per-source dashboard). Multi-source matters: dashboards are built on relationships; wants a flow from seeing how sources relate to building a dashboard on a slice. Wants to see which sources existing dashboards cover. Relationship/ERD view is a different action from the source hover/click.

Hover card about a third of the viewport (~400x400): full summary width, rows scroll; no charts. Clicking a value: pick a sensible default, Byron will give feedback. Save writes an .eda file. Explorer is a dashboard against just that one source; multi-source scope belongs to the schema view. Next: 3-4 strongly different HTML mockups built on the live app, shown as images.

Chose mockup A: full Fields card on hover; click shows summary beside rows; value click filters and re-describes (like an unsaved analysis). B guesses three charts, worse than all fields. C compact card and rows-only rejected. D rail tree rejected: layout shift, and a narrow rail is the wrong place to explore; a full schema/field view needs its own dedicated view.
